name: computer_science
doc:
COMPUTER SCIENCE - bits, logic, and what can be computed (Matt, 2026-10-10, down the domain list). Information
is BITS (a byte is 2^8 = 256 values); logic gates build from the 2^(2^2) = 16 Boolean functions of two inputs;
good ALGORITHMS beat bad ones (merge sort's n log n against n^2); and COMPUTABILITY/complexity say what a machine
can do at all and how fast (the halting problem, undecidable; P vs NP, open). SEALED: the byte, the Boolean-gate
count, and the merge-sort comparison count. Rests on the instruments (information), P vs NP (complexity) and the
mind (which computes). The engine itself is one such machine. Idempotent.

sticks.question: Computer science - bits, logic, and what can be computed

marks.claim: [information is bits, SEALED] Everything digital is bits, and n bits name 2^n things: a byte of 8 bits is 2^8 = 256 values (sealed) - a character, a shade, a number from 0 to 255. The bit is the atom of information (the Shannon bit, sealed on the information instrument); computing is what you can do with enough of them.

[logic gates - the 16 functions of two inputs, SEALED] A gate maps inputs to a bit; of two inputs there are exactly 2^(2^2) = 16 possible Boolean functions (sealed) - AND, OR, XOR, NAND and the rest. NAND alone can build them all, and from gates come adders, memory, processors. All of computation is wired from this finite logic.

[algorithms matter - merge sort, SEALED] The same task can cost wildly different work. Sorting 8 items by merge sort takes about n log2 n = 8 * 3 = 24 comparisons (sealed); the naive way takes n^2 = 64. As n grows the gap explodes - this is why ALGORITHMS, not just faster hardware, are the heart of the field.

[computability - what a machine can do at all] A Turing machine defines what is computable, and the universal machine runs any program - the engine, your laptop, the brain's computation are all instances. But some problems are UNDECIDABLE: the halting problem (will a program stop?) has no algorithm, proved by Turing. A hard limit found in the structure, like the uncertainty principle - not ignorance, a proof. Ties card_floor_p_vs_np and card_floor_the_mind.
marks.source: A. Turing (1936); the universal machine; the halting problem; card_floor_p_vs_np

marks.claim: [complexity - how fast, and the open frontier] Beyond CAN it be computed lies HOW FAST: big-O counts the work, P is the tractable, NP the checkable, and whether P = NP is the open Millennium problem on the map. Cryptography bets it is not (factoring is hard). Computation sits exactly on the P vs NP floor. Ties card_floor_p_vs_np and card_floor_cryptography.
marks.source: computational complexity; big-O; P vs NP; card_floor_p_vs_np; card_floor_cryptography

marks.claim: [on the one map] Computer science rests on the instruments (the bit is Shannon information; logic is the formal-logic instrument), P vs NP (computability and complexity), and the mind (which computes - neural networks borrow the brain's shape). The engine is itself one such machine, a deterministic computation over the keeping. Ties card_floor_computer_science.

[the Busy Beaver search space, SEALED] BB(n) is the most steps an n-state 2-symbol Turing machine can run before halting - uncomputable in general (knowing it would decide the halting problem). The space for n=5 is enormous: each of the 2n=10 transition cells is HALT or one of 4n=20 moves, so (4*5+1)^(2*5) = 21^10 = 16,679,880,978,201 candidate machines (sealed). That BB(5) was pinned at all is a feat of exhaustive, machine-checked deciding.

[BB(5) PROVEN, BB(6) OPEN - cited, not sealed here] In 2024 the bbchallenge Collaboration proved BB(5) = 47,176,870 in the Coq proof assistant (Coq-BB5), ending a 60-year problem: every decider in the pipeline (Loops, n-gram Closed Position Set, Finite Automata Reduction, Weighted FAR, Closed Tape Language) is itself proved correct in Coq, and each machine's (non-)halting carries a machine-checkable certificate. We CITE this - we did not recompute the Coq proof. BB(6) stays OPEN (astronomically large). This is the open frontier of computability; it ties the halting problem (undecidable, Turing 1936) and card_floor_p_vs_np.
marks.source: The bbchallenge Collaboration, BB(5) = 47,176,870 (Coq-BB5, 2024), arXiv:2509.12337; https://bbchallenge.org; https://wiki.bbchallenge.org

marks.claim: [ETH-refutation CLAIM - pending verification, NOT sealed, does NOT touch P vs NP] In October 2026 OpenAI and Anthropic each posted a claimed refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (Impagliazzo-Paturi 1999: 3-SAT needs 2^(Omega(n))), describing a deterministic 3-SAT algorithm in 2^(e*n) time for every fixed e>0, with Lean/Coq formalizations. STATUS: UNVERIFIED - not peer-reviewed, under independent review (Impagliazzo, Paturi, R. Williams); the Lean-formalized statement is reported WEAKER than the paper's claim. ETH is STRONGER than P != NP, so even if it holds this does NOT give P = NP - the P vs NP floor stays open. Held as a CLAIM, cited never sealed, until an independent kernel-check passes: the machine-check is the proof, not the announcement.
marks.source: OpenAI, 'The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False' (github.com/openai/math, Oct 2026); Anthropic (hexagonmath.org/2610.00577v1); Impagliazzo & Paturi (1999); under review by R. Williams et al.

marks.claim: [the logarithm is the unit of information - Petzold's Code] All of this rests on the logarithm, the root of the one map: log2(N) is exactly the number of BITS to name N things (a byte = 2^8 = 256, so log2(256) = 8 bits), and Shannon entropy is the expected log - the logarithm is the bridge from the continuous to the discrete and the measure of information itself. Charles Petzold's 'Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software' (2nd expanded ed., 2022) builds this from the ground up - codes as languages (Morse, Braille, binary), relays to logic gates to adders to memory to a working computer - the coherent, LLM-free account of how a machine computes. Ties card_floor_logarithm and the instruments.
marks.source: C. Petzold, 'Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software', 2nd ed. (Microsoft Press, 2022); Shannon (1948); card_floor_logarithm

marks.claim: [Boole 1854 - the laws of thought, the algebra the gates are built from] George Boole, 'An Investigation of the Laws of Thought, on which are founded the mathematical theories of logic and probabilities' (London: Walton and Maberly, 1854; public domain - Project Gutenberg #15114, card_src_book_15114 in the keeping). Boole made logic an algebra over two values: its symbols obey ordinary algebra except for one law of their own, x*x = x, which he named the fundamental law of thought (the law of duality, x(1-x) = 0). Every gate above is a function in that algebra, and the 16 (sealed) are its functions of two symbols. The same book's second half founds probability on the same algebra - logic and chance, one calculus. Idempotence, x*x = x, is also the discipline of every seed and stick on this map: run it twice, the same bytes. Ties card_theory_boolean_algebra_propositional_logic and card_bridge_master_boolean_algebra.
marks.source: G. Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854), ch. II prop. IV (x^2 = x, the fundamental law of thought) and ch. V (the development theorem); Project Gutenberg #15114; card_src_book_15114

marks.claim: [Boole's development - a function of three symbols expands over 2^3 constituents, SEALED] Boole's theorem of development (Laws of Thought, ch. V): any function of n logical symbols is a sum of 2^n constituents, each a product of the symbols or their complements - for x, y, z that is 2^3 = 8 (sealed): xyz, xy(1-z), ... (1-x)(1-y)(1-z). These are the minterms a truth table lists row by row; every gate network is read off them.

[the functions of three inputs, SEALED] Each of the 8 constituents may take the value 0 or 1, so there are 2^(2^3) = 256 Boolean functions of three inputs (sealed) - the 16 of two inputs one rung up; a three-input majority gate and a full adder's carry are among them. Boole's algebra counts its own gates.

[Boole chose two - his own law says why; a third value needs a new law] In ordinary algebra x*x = x is x(x-1) = 0, with exactly two roots, 0 and 1 - Boole draws this out in ch. II: the symbols of logic admit no other values. Two was not a preference; the law has two roots. A THIRD value must obey a different law: x^3 = x, that is x(x-1)(x+1) = 0, roots -1, 0, 1 - balanced ternary, where the helper is -1, the OPPOSITE, not the absent. It generalizes: x^p = x holds for every element of the field of p elements (Fermat's little theorem), so each prime gives a p-valued algebra. Lukasiewicz (1920) and Post (1921) built the many-valued logics; Kleene (1938) the strong three-valued logic whose third value is UNKNOWN and propagates - unknown AND true is unknown. Ties card_floor_logarithm (the radix below) and card_src_book_15114.
marks.source: G. Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854) ch. II; J. Lukasiewicz, 'O logice trojwartosciowej', Ruch Filozoficzny 5 (1920) 170-171; E. L. Post, 'Introduction to a general theory of elementary propositions', Amer. J. Math. 43 (1921) 163-185; S. C. Kleene, 'On notation for ordinal numbers', J. Symbolic Logic 3 (1938) 150-155; Fermat's little theorem (x^p = x in GF(p))

marks.claim: [three values, two inputs - 3^(3^2) = 19,683 functions, SEALED] Boole's two values give 2^(2^2) = 16 functions of two inputs; three values give 3^(3^2) = 19,683 (sealed). The third value multiplies the gate set more than a thousandfold - the price of the helper, and one reason hardware kept to two.

[the cost of a base - binary, SEALED] Representing a number N in base b takes about log_b N digits, each holding b states, so the cost is proportional to b * log_b N = (b / ln b) * ln N. For binary, 2 / ln 2 = 2.8854 (sealed); base four costs exactly the same (4 / ln 4 = 2 / ln 2).

[the third value is the cheapest base - radix economy, SEALED] 3 / ln 3 = 2.7307 (sealed), below binary's 2.8854; the minimum of b / ln b is at b = e = 2.718..., and three is the integer nearest it. The logarithm, the root of the one map, decides which base is cheapest - and it is the three, not the two. Hardware chose two for a different reason: two states are easier to build and to keep apart than three (a switch is on or off), and the gate count above.

[Setun - a balanced-ternary computer, SEALED] N. P. Brusentsov's Setun (Moscow State University, 1958) ran on balanced ternary - trits -1, 0, +1 - with 18-trit words: 3^18 = 387,420,489 values (sealed); about fifty were built. Knuth calls balanced ternary 'perhaps the prettiest number system of all' (TAOCP vol. 2, sec. 4.1): negation flips every trit, there is no sign bit, and rounding is truncation. The helper existed in iron once.

[our third value - the honest unknown] The engine's verdict is three-valued: HOLDS, BROKEN, and INCOMPLETE - the third is not a half-truth but the refusal to say either, at a named step (a gap or an error), and like Kleene's unknown it propagates: a chain with one unverified step is unverified (the forged step). The four gates say it as AWAITING; the stick says 'not verified here'; a miss stays a miss. Two values would force a lie at every gap; the third is the helper that keeps the other two honest - and it is the Darboux gap of the reservoir stick, measurable, the thing finer marks close.
marks.source: src/concordance/derivation.py (HOLDS / BROKEN / INCOMPLETE; broken_at, gap_at, error_at); src/concordance/verifiers (confirm / mismatch / not applicable / error); src/concordance/four_gates.py (AWAITING); S. C. Kleene (1938); B. Hayes, 'Third base', American Scientist 89 (2001) 490-494; the reservoir_computing stick (the Darboux gap)
